pr.title: Draw the band as one panel on a background that follows the theme
pr.head: 7d067a8bb13b376078bdc8af4979b9a96d20238d

summary: Projector's band is the strip a Claude Code plugin draws above the prompt. It lists the session's tracked pull requests and the inbox's questions and notices, one line each. In a terminal, it used to draw those rows straight onto the transcript's background, under a ─ divider that held the counts and the time since the last reload. When the band scrolled, you could not easily tell which lines were the band's.

This change draws the band, in a terminal only, as one panel with a background of its own. The panel is inset one column from the terminal's edge and ends at bodyColumns, the column where Claude Code draws the band's [-] collapse mark. A header replaces the divider: /projector at its left, and the counts and the reload's age at its right, all in the theme's subtle color. The pull requests and items sit two columns in from each side of the panel, and the header one column in. A key hint takes the panel's last row: ctrl+x tab to focus while the prompt has the keyboard, and esc to return · enter to open once the band has it. The header's age, each row's age, and the hint end in one column.

The background follows the Claude Code theme, a step darker than the terminal so the panel reads as sunken. A new panel.background setting in .projector.toml overrides it. Claude Desktop, VS Code, and the mobile app draw as before, with no panel and no header.

groups.title: A setting for the panel's color
groups.kicker: The CLI learns the panel.background key, so config set and unset change it.
intro: project config reads and writes Projector's settings in .projector.toml files, layered from the repository out to ~/.projector.toml. It only sets keys listed in SETTINGS. This group adds panel.background as a string, so you can set it with project config set panel.background 'rgb(30,30,40)' --user, and documents it in the settings table.

files.note: Sets, reads, and unsets the key the way the band reads it, with --default auto --json.
Adds the key to the settings table.

groups.title: The band draws as one panel
groups.kicker: register.tsx picks the panel's color and wraps every layout of the band in it.
intro: The band is drawn by a ui.render handler for Claude Code's AbovePrompt component in hooks/register.tsx. It has three layouts: the list of pull requests and items, an open item's drawer, which has the band to itself, and the empty band with its tagline. This group wraps all three in one panel() helper. In a terminal, it nests an inset Box, a padded Box with a backgroundColor, the header (left out for a drawer), a rows Box padded one more column at each side, and the key hint.

The color is kept in two state atoms so the render never waits on a read. bandThemeBackground holds the theme's color, written at session start from $.config.list() and again on each config.set of theme. bandBackground holds the setting, read with project config get once just after start and on every reload. The render uses the setting unless it is auto.

Claude Code refuses a plugin's whole render tree over a color it will not accept, which would make the band disappear. So readBackground checks the setting against PAINTABLE, a pattern of at most 40 letters, digits, and #(),.%_ -, and falls back to auto with one toast for a value that fails it.

The hint changes when the keyboard moves. A ui.focus hook on the band marks it focused in the isBandFocused atom and redraws the band. Claude Code raises no event when Esc returns the keyboard to the prompt. So unfocus clears the mark at the next keystroke in the prompt, from the prompt.edit hook. It also clears it when you send a prompt from the terminal, from the prompt.submit hook. Neither hook waits on the redraw.

checks.text: In a throwaway test under Claude Code 2.1.299's test engine, a Box background was refused for exactly the values PAINTABLE rejects that were tried (ansi:black, the empty string, 41 characters), and accepted for about 20 odd values it passes, such as rgb(1, 2, 3), %, and a 40-character name.

files.note: Adds the panel constants, the theme lookup, the setting read, the theme and focus hooks, and the panel() helper with its header, rows box, and key hint.

checks.text: The pattern mirrors what the engine refuses, not what it can paint. A name the engine accepts but does not know, such as a misspelled theme key, passes here; the review asked whether a real terminal then draws no background.
A custom theme's slug comes from Claude Code's own theme setting, and the file read stays under the Claude config directory; an unreadable file gives inverseText.
This adds one project config get process to every reload: every 30 seconds while the band is shown, and at the end of each turn.

Traced: the panel is bodyColumns - 1 wide, padded one column at each side, and the rows box pads one more, so rows are columns = bodyColumns - 5 wide. The header and hint are edgeColumns = columns + 1 wide and start a column further left, so all three end in one column; a new test pins it.

Traced and tested: unfocus runs only for a prompt sent from the terminal, detached so the send never waits on it. It redraws the band only when the mark was set, and the hint test's second send adds no redraw.

files.note: Declares the three new state atoms: bandThemeBackground, bandBackground, and isBandFocused.

Pins the panel's shape, the header, the color for each theme and custom theme, a theme change, the setting as written, and the fallback toasts; updates every divider assertion to the header. Adds tests for the key hint's two states and redraws, and for the header, row, and hint ages ending in one column.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: plugins.md describes the panel and the setting; the inbox plan records the decision.
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the band for users. It now explains the panel, the color per theme, the header, the key hint, and a new section on choosing the panel's color, with its examples redrawn. The inbox plan, already completed, gains § 20, which records what changed, why the owner chose a sunken, theme-picked background over inverseText and fixed greys, and which test pins each behavior.
